Maya (SRE): Hey — seeing intermittent failures calling model-service via the VPCE in eu-west-1 after we migrated a few ASGs to the new subnet range. Some pods timeout talking to the endpoint.
Maya (SRE): Errors are TCP RST or connect timeout, not app-level 5xx. Suspect networking layer (VPCE/route53/SG). :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy model-service@2026-11-09T10:34:12 completed in eu-west-1 (no infra changes)
Ben (Infra): Can you paste a dig + traceroute from one of the failing pods? Also need the VPC endpoint describe output.
Maya (SRE): paste below — pod from new subnet (10.1.44.0/20)
```;
<<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> model-service.vpce.internal
;; ANSWER SECTION:
model-service.vpce.internal. 300 IN CNAME vpce-abc123-xxxxxxxx.eu-west-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.
vpce-abc123-xxxxxxxx.eu-west-1.vpce.amazonaws.com. 300 IN A 10.0.12.34
```
```
$ traceroute -n 10.0.12.34
1  10.1.44.1  0.4 ms
2  10.1.0.1   0.7 ms
3  * * *
```
Maya (SRE): AWS describe-vpc-endpoints for vpce-abc123 shows ENI in subnet 10.0.12.0/24 (old AZ/subnet). The endpoint exists and ENI is healthy.
Ashley (NetEng): That A record points to the ENI IP in the old subnet. Did the private hosted zone get re-associated to the new VPC when you spun up the new subnets? If the private hosted zone is only linked to the old VPC, then DNS will keep resolving to the old ENI IP.
Ben (Infra): Also double-check endpoint SGs — if the endpoint SG allows only the old CIDR (10.0.0.0/16) and the new subnets are 10.1.0.0/16, that would cause connections to be dropped even if DNS resolved to the new ENI later.
Kai (Oncall): Ran route53 list-hosted-zones --query to check associations, here's trimmed output: 
```HostedZoneId: Z0EXAMPLE
Name: vpce.amazonaws.com
VPCs:
 - VPCRegion: eu-west-1
   VPCId: vpc-aaaa1111   <-- old VPC only
```
Kai (Oncall): New VPC id is vpc-bbbb2222 (the migration target). It is not associated.
Maya (SRE): OK that matches what we see — DNS still resolving to ENI in vpc-aaaa1111. Why wasn't the hosted zone association carried during the migration?
Ashley (NetEng): Looks like our automated migration playbook skipped the route53 association step when creating the new VPC peering/migration. Two fixes: 1) associate the private hosted zone with the new VPC; 2) update endpoint SGs to include the new subnet CIDR/more explicit SG references.
Ben (Infra): Steps I executed: 
```aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=eu-west-1,VPCId=vpc-bbbb2222
aws ec2 modify-network-interface-attribute --network-interface-id eni-0abcd --groups sg-ep-old sg-ep-new
```
Ben (Infra): After associating the hosted zone, the CNAME stayed the same but the A record resolved to a new IP in 10.1.44. (propagated quickly — TTL 300).
Maya (SRE): Confirming DNS now: 
```model-service.vpce.internal. 300 IN CNAME vpce-abc123-xxxxxxxx.eu-west-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.
vpce-abc123-xxxxxxxx.eu-west-1.vpce.amazonaws.com. 60 IN A 10.1.44.55
```
Maya (SRE): Test connection from pod -> success, no timeouts.
Kai (Oncall): Root cause: hosted zone association missing + endpoint SG didn't include new subnet. Contributing factor: our migration playbook didn't assert route53 association or use SG-by-reference (we use CIDRs).
Ashley (NetEng): Action items: 
- Add hosted zone association step to the migration playbook and a post-check that the VPCE A resolves to ENI in the target subnets.
- Switch endpoint SGs to reference workload SGs instead of CIDR ranges where possible.
- Add an automated test in staging that reassigns a pod to a different subnet and asserts VPCE connectivity.
Maya (SRE): I'll open a ticket for the migration playbook and add the post-check snippet.
Ben (Infra): Ticket created: INFRA-2418 (add route53 association and SG ref checks)
Maya (SRE): Thanks all — marking this thread resolved for now. :thumbsup:
Ashley (NetEng): Nice catch. We should also add an alert for VPCE DNS/CNAME -> ENI IP mismatch after major network changes.
Kai (Oncall): Noted, will add to runbook.
Maya (SRE): closing out — will verify infra automation tomorrow during the next staged migration.
